messages:
jules (customer): Hey, seeing a streaming response from the API that cuts off mid-JSON. client-side parse failing — final bytes are missing. Repro steps + curl below. Anyone seen this with proxies in front of the app?

jules (customer): curl command we used:
```
curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?mode=json\"
```
The last chunk we get ends like: `...\"items\": [{\"id\":\"a1\",\"val\":\"x\"}]` and then connection closes — missing closing `\n` and overall trailing bracket for outer object.

maria (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the raw bytes (hex or curl --trace) and confirm if you have any CDN/proxy (Cloudflare, Fastly, nginx LB) in front? Also which SDK/version?

jules (customer): We're behind Cloudflare + an internal nginx reverse proxy. SDK is our own Node fetch wrapper. Attaching the last 200 bytes from curl --trace-ascii: 
```
* Received data chunk: 132 bytes
data: {"type":"delta","content":"..."}
* Received data chunk: 64 bytes
data: {"type":"delta","content":"..."}
* Received data chunk: 7 bytes
data: {"type":"delta","content":"}
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact
```
So you can see the last chunk ends mid-string (`\"content\":\"`) and then closes.

sam (eng-runtime): That pattern (last chunk short, then connection close) looks like an upstream FIN before the final chunk/frame is flushed. Possible causes: early keepalive timeouts on the proxy, or a middleware that buffers and then closes without sending final chunk marker. Does your nginx have `proxy_buffering on` or `proxy_read_timeout` set low? Also Cloudflare has a 100s idle timeout on some plans.

alex (eng-sre): Can you run one more trace capturing TCP-level events? `curl --trace-ascii dump.txt -N ...` is good; better is `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w capture.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443` (or run on the proxy hop). Need to verify if TLS shutdown happens with FIN or RST. If it's RST, likely proxy is killing the connection. If FIN, the server closed cleanly but didn't finish the SSE framing.

jules (customer): I grabbed the nginx access/error tail. Error shows: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream`. nginx config has `proxy_read_timeout 60s`. Our stream can be idle-ish between deltas, so maybe hitting that.

maria (support): Two immediate suggestions while you gather captures: 1) try adding a short heartbeat from the server (every ~10s) so idle intervals don't look like idle to proxies. 2) set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` / `Cache-Control: no-transform` on the response to avoid buffering.

sam (eng-runtime): Agreed. On our side, we've seen Cloudflare or certain LBs coalesce and drop the final chunk if the origin closes the TLS session before the kernel flushes the socket. Workarounds: flush frequently from the app (fsync-equivalent in runtime), or ensure the server writes the SSE `data: {\"type\":\"done\"}\\n\n` final event and then waits ~200ms before closing. Also adding `Connection: keep-alive` may help.

jules (customer): Will try heartbeats + increase proxy_read_timeout to 300s and report back. Quick question: is there anything Redwood can do server-side to avoid this for hosted customers?

sam (eng-runtime): We can add a streaming keepalive event for customers on hosted by default for JSON-mode streams, but need to validate cost/behavior. I'll open an internal bug to discuss defaulting to heartbeat frames.

alex (eng-sre): Also will check if our edge proxy is sending `FIN` early for certain connection termination paths. If we find a bug we'll patch and notify impacted customers.

jules (customer): I applied heartbeat and raised read timeout — initial smoke looks better, haven't seen truncation in 30m. Thanks. :relieved:

maria (support): Great — marking as workaround validated. We'll keep this thread open while backend teams investigate the root cause and consider default heartbeat on hosted. If you can share the tcpdump or pcap we requested (sanitized) that would help.

edgebot (deploy-bot): deploy: edge/proxy 2026-03-17T14:02 UTC — rolling update started.

sam (eng-runtime): noted — will watch to ensure the deploy doesn't affect ongoing traces.

maria (support): Thanks all — next steps: jules to upload pcap if truncation reoccurs, eng-runtime to open internal issue for heartbeat default, eng-sre to review edge proxy FIN/RST behavior. I'll follow up in 24h. :eyes:
